pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to Our School - Castlebar Primary School
pageCache.text:
It gives me immense pride to welcome you to this outstanding Local Authority special school, dedicated to children aged 4-11 years old with complex learning difficulties, including autism and other sensory impairments. Our school is a nurturing environment where every child is valued and supported, even those with challenging behaviours.
At Castlebar, we take immense pride in our pupil’s achievements. Our children make remarkable progress, particularly in communication, independence, and socialisation. They are truly exceptional, and we are committed to providing them with the best possible education and care.
Our staff are not only hardworking and dedicated but also highly skilled. They collaborate with other professionals to ensure that our school offers the highest quality provision. We believe in a strong partnership with our parents and carers, working together to support each child’s journey through Castlebar School.
Whether you are an existing Castlebar parent, a new parent seeking the right school for your child, or a teacher/support staff looking for your next career opportunity, I hope you find all the information you need here. If you have any questions or suggestions for additional information on our website, please do not hesitate to contact us.

During term time, Castlebar runs a limited number of clubs for children aged 7 – 11 to attend.Please contact the school office for availability and any related costs.
Basketball Club
A professional coach takes this club which works o a range of ball skills and teamwork.
Bike Club
Children wear cycle helmets and can cycle around the playground on a range of bicycles.
Cooking Club
Children cook and prepare simple dishes and treats.
Cricket Club
Cricket for Change run this club which focuses on coordination skills, social skills and fun!
Football Club
A coach teaches football skills and they play mini tournaments with the children.

Our school meals are provided by ISS. They have a diverse menu that runs on a 3 week rota, with vegetarian options everyday.
To pay for your school meals please see our online payment page.
See below for the guide on how to pay.
If you are eligible for free school meals or require further information on this please click on the link:Free School Meals
Or please contact Pupil Support Services at Ealing by calling: 020 8825 5566 or Email Pupilsupport@ealing.gov.uk
Please note that pupils in reception, year 1 and year 2 currently receive a universal free school meal (UFSM), this is different from benefit driven free school meals. Please do still apply for free school meals as the school receives additional funding to support pupils on the free school meals register. This funding is known as pupil premium. For further information on pupil premium see http://castlebar.ealing.sch.uk/our-school/pupil-premium/
If you need support with your application the school social worker may be able to help.

IEP Targets
Each child will receive a termly Individual Education Plan (IEP) with clear targets to work on both at school and home. The plan outlines ‘Support at home’ and includes strategies and activities that will support your child to achieve their target. Parents/carers are encouraged to work with their child on these targets weekly.
Reading Books

pageCache.pageTitle: Health and Safety - Castlebar Primary School
pageCache.text:
We take pupil security very seriously. School gates are closed at 9.05 am and our children are supervised at all times.
Health Care Plans for children can be arranged as required and we liaise closely with parents and carers regarding any allergies, illness and prescribed medicines from the doctor.
Castlebar has a behaviour policy for the school and some pupils will have Behaviour Management Plans to help to structure their behaviour. Team Teach training for staff runs throughout the school so staff use practiced techniques to keep pupils safe should they become distressed.

pageCache.pageTitle: Parent and Carer Support - Castlebar Primary School
pageCache.text:
Who to Call
If you are unsure who you need to get in contact with you can refer to our new chart!
Our Parent/School Communication and Contacts chart shows you who to call for what situation.
Parent and Carer Workshops
Castlebar School places strong emphasis on working together with parents and carers. We offer a range of parent and carer programmes, workshops and coffee mornings throughout the academic year. We aim to provide a range of services that encompass both educational and practical sessions, as well as opportunities for parents to share their own knowledge and expertise and gain support from one another.
The Parent and Carer Brochure has been produced to help promote the programmes that will be offered during the Autumn and Spring Term. Click the button below to view the brochure. If you have any feedback or interest in a specific topic, please share them with Heather England.
Teaching/Learning Workshops
During the year Castlebar School offers a range of workshops to support the work done in school around communication, socialisation and independence. For example, teachers/staff run reading and counting workshops or communication/ICT workshops. For some more information on reading please see Oxford Owl
Ealing Transport Assistance
Ealing Council offers home to school travel assistance for eligible children and young people with special educational needs/ and or disability (SEND).
If you wish to apply you can find out more about how to apply by clicking this link.
If you wish to apply for travel assistance you can fill in Ealing’s form.
If your child or young person already accesses travel assistance your contact is below:
Ealing Council has a statutory responsibility to provide travel assistance to children living in the borough with SEN as well as children with other significant obstacles that may prevent them from reaching their educational setting
Additional Specialist Support
Castlebar also have our own dedicated School Social Worker, Occupational Therapist and Speech and Language Therapist.
Ealing Family Support Services – Quick Guide
Download the Quick Guide to Ealing Family Support Services below – A guide to services provided by Ealing Council and immediate partners for children, young people and families.
Ealing Help
Ealing Help Events Calendar – has details of many events from leisure activities to parenting courses.
Ealing Parent & Carer Forum
If you care for a child or young adult with additional needs in education, health or social care the Ealing Parent & Carer Forum is for you. The forum works to ensure Ealing Council, local health and other service providers understand what your children and young adults really need to deliver the support that is so essential to their development.
CEPPS
CEPPS provides advice, information and support to parents/carers of children with special educational needs (SEN) with their children’s education. Advice is free, impartial and confidential.

pageCache.pageTitle: Family Support Noticeboard - Castlebar Primary School
pageCache.text:
We have an online notice board for Castlebar families to learn about support that can be accessed within our school and in the local community. It details a range of workshops, supporting organisations and social opportunities to meet other families of SEND children. We regularly update the noticeboard to highlight key resources and events that may be of interest to our families.
Our main school website is still the main place to head to for information relating to Castlebar School specifically, and Ealing’s Local Offer website should be used for the most up to date information on all the services and provision available to children and families in the Borough who are living with Special Educational Needs.
Please do bookmark the Castlebar Family Support Noticeboard and keep checking it for regular updates. If you have any suggestions on what you would like to see featured please contact the Family Support Team at Castlebar.
